items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: We did those things at Bob Festein's studio

ctx.x: You have to. They prefer it now because they get through faster, they don't have to spend so much time in the studio that way. Everybody likes it better; certainly the entrepreneurs like it better. So you're pretty much forced to use a click track. If you try not to, the acoustics in the room foil you.

I tried not to out there and I couldn't, because nobody could hear you, either my stick is not clear enough or they're not used to following it anymore. It was all over the place and the only way to bring it together was the click track. That didn't happen in New York, but the engineer has a lot to do with that, how he places people.
